tagline: Up the valley's west edge, with the aqueduct alongside.
intro: North of Highway 152 and the San Luis Reservoir, Interstate 5 runs up the far western edge of the San Joaquin Valley along the eastern foothills of the Diablo Range, well away from the valley's larger towns. The California Aqueduct keeps it company, and the freeway crosses it twice along here, once between 152 and Highway 33 and again near Crows Landing. South of Tracy, I-580 splits off toward the Bay Area and carries the designation on to I-205 near Altamont Raceway Park.
The freeway took over an older line. Through Santa Nella, it and Highway 33 replaced the route of El Camino Viejo.

moments.title: Santa Nella
moments.text: The name is a corruption of centinela, not a saint, after the Sentinel Ranch of 1810, which became a stopping place for stages and travelers on El Camino Viejo.

moments.title: Del Puerto Canyon
moments.text: Del Puerto Creek's canyon falls from 2,800 feet at its head, on the south slope of Red Mountain, to 223 feet at its mouth.
